description: OrbitFire AI is building an AI-powered solution for the Flame in Freefall challenge using NASA microgravity combustion data. Our goal is to turn complex fire experiments into clear insights for future space safety. I bring experience in full-stack development, Python, AI/ML, and data analysis. We are looking for teammates skilled in AI, data science, UI/UX, space science, visualization, and presentation.
summary:
OrbitFire is an interactive prototype that makes NASA microgravity combustion research easier to explore. Users search six curated evidence records from NASA publications, filter research topics, compare experimental context, and download source-linked evidence briefs.

The dashboard brings together information about atmosphere, materials, suppression, and smoke detection. Each record includes its source and limitations, helping readers distinguish reported observations from research implications.

This initial version uses transparent keyword ranking and templated summaries. Live AI synthesis and raw experimental dataset integration are future work. OrbitFire aims to support education and more informed exploration of fire safety research for spacecraft and future habitats.
details:
NASA’s microgravity combustion research spans multiple experiments and publications. OrbitFire helps readers explore this knowledge while preserving the context and limitations of each source.

The prototype contains six curated records covering Saffire-V, Saffire-VI, BASS, FLEX, and SAME. Users can search keywords, filter topics, adjust the relevance weight of atmosphere records, compare selected findings, and export an evidence brief with NASA source links.

Built using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, the application runs in a browser without API keys or installation. Its relevance scores rank documents; they do not estimate fire risk. Briefs use fixed templates and curated publication summaries.

The intended benefit is to make research easier to navigate for students and research teams. Its design places evidence, experimental context, and limitations together.

This is an early prototype. It does not currently ingest raw experimental measurements, run a live AI model, or provide validated fire predictions. Next steps include NASA Physical Sciences Informatics dataset integration, source-grounded AI synthesis, and scientific validation.

ChatGPT/Codex assisted with source discovery, publication summaries, application code, and documentation. NASA resources are credited individually. This independent project is not NASA-endorsed.
